Ram needs power to store. If you put your computer to sleep the RAM is still powered to maintain storage. If you put it into hibernate the data on RAM is written on disk and then stored back into RAM once power is restored.

Persistent data stores are inherently slow; technological advances has made this quicker, but it'll always be a fact of life. RAM work as fast as it does because it's entirely ephemeral: by foregoing any lasting effects, the data store can be adjusted far faster.

However, what you're thinking of in that first sentence isn't entirely irrelevant: modern operating systems will read large amounts of data from the disk into RAM in order to work with it far faster than otherwise possible(with changes being flushed to disk every so often). There's also the concept of the RAM disk(a logical device with no actual disk backing it up).

The reason RAM isn't going away is because it doesn't wear out as fast as solid states would at that usage rate (last I checked anyways, there was something about SSDs being used as RAM, but I never followed up on how long they'd last). Anyways, having a dedicated section of memory will probably always be better than using disk space, although what will probably happen is the lines get blurred between RAM and disks because someone is going to want to compact them and move them so close together that they look like one thing
